components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Guide-light primary action for task creation, form submission, and successful control return.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent, #c8ff00); color: #000; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px 16px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.85; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #c8ff00); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action for cancellation, accounts access, and quiet controls.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--muted, #666); border: 1px solid var(--border, #222); border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px 12px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #555; color: var(--text, #e8e8e8); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #c8ff00); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: Vigil's interface is an operator room for autonomous browser work: dark, dense, and precise, but not hostile. The system uses compact mono typography, quiet graphite surfaces, and one rare guide-light accent to keep attention on task state, live browser evidence, and the next available intervention. The design should preserve the existing operational efficiency while softening intimidation. It rejects black-box terminal theatrics, decorative SaaS gloss, and vague status presentation.
keyCharacteristics: Compact five-column workflow with persistent task state.
Dark tonal surfaces separated by thin borders rather than heavy shadows.
Rare neon-lime action color reserved for primary actions, active values, and reports.
Semantic status colors for task lifecycle and human handoff.
Mono-forward typography that reads as transparent and inspectable.

rules.name: The Guide-Light Rarity Rule
rules.body: The primary accent should occupy less than 10% of any screen. If everything glows, nothing is actionable.

rules.name: The State Color Rule
rules.body: Blue, amber, green, red, and queue gray are semantic colors, not decoration. Do not reuse them for unrelated emphasis.

rules.name: The Mono Transparency Rule
rules.body: Use JetBrains Mono across UI labels, controls, and data so agent actions feel inspectable. Do not introduce display fonts into product controls.

rules.name: The Compact Scale Rule
rules.body: Product UI headings stay fixed-size and compact. Do not use fluid hero typography in the dashboard.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Focused Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Lift is allowed only when the user is focused on a modal, drawer, or manual-control state.

dos: Do preserve the Soft Control Room posture: operational, calm, and readable under task pressure.
Do use Guide Light sparingly for primary action, focus, and completion/report emphasis.
Do keep task lifecycle colors semantic and consistent across dots, labels, banners, and buttons.
Do maintain visible focus states on every control, especially modal fields and manual-control inputs.
Do use empty states and error copy to explain what the operator can do next.
donts: Don't create an intimidating black-box terminal aesthetic; the UI is for AI operators, not only low-level debuggers.
Don't add generic bright SaaS polish, gradient text, glassmorphism, or decorative metrics.
Don't hide important state transitions behind vague labels or color-only cues.
Don't use colored side-stripe borders wider than 1px as accents on cards, callouts, or alerts.
Don't introduce display fonts, large fluid headings, or marketing-page hero patterns inside the dashboard.
